normalized.governing_thought: Harlow can lift operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028 by fixing promotions, shrink and delivery pricing instead of cutting store hours across the board
executive_summary: Wages are not the main cause: promotions, shrink and e-commerce explain 87% of the margin fall since FY2023 – Operating margin fell from 3.37% to 1.02% in two years; store labor explains only 13% of it (p. 4, 5)
An 8% cut in store hours would miss the target and put fresh produce at risk – A shrink rise like that of FY2023–25 would erase about half of its $14.5M saving (p. 7, 8)
Promotions are the largest lever, worth 0.7 percentage points of margin – Returning to 24% of sales needs cuts only among the 38% of events that lose money (p. 10–12)

Home delivery lost about $10M in FY2025; the tested pricing keeps the service and saves about $2.5M a year – The team's 6.1% margin leaves out delivery costs and counts every online sale as new (p. 14–16)
Five moves reach about 3.2% by FY2028, and the three that need no capital come first to clear the covenant – The 2027 minimum-wage rise, up to $7.3M a year, is the main risk to the plan (p. 18–21)

Executive summary

slides.title: What drove the decline
Promotions, shrink and e-commerce fulfillment, not wages, explain 87% of the fall in operating margin since FY2023

claims.claim: 87% of the fall in operating margin comes from promotions, shrink and e-commerce fulfillment
evidence: Waterfall: FY2023 3.37%; Promotions −0.70 pp; Private label +0.18 pp; Shrink −0.50 pp; E-commerce fulfillment −0.84 pp; Store labor −0.30 pp; Occupancy −0.20 pp; FY2025 1.02%

claims.claim: E-commerce fulfillment: the largest step
evidence: its cost grew 3.5 times as orders grew 2.9 times and more went to the home

claims.claim: Promotions: promotional sales earn 14 percentage points less margin, and their share of sales kept rising
Shrink: fresh waste, theft and receiving errors took a larger share of every sales dollar
Store labor: only 13% of the fall, despite being management's main explanation
Promotions, private label and shrink account for the whole fall in gross margin; other SG&A was unchanged as a share of sales

slides.title: Wage inflation was largely absorbed: labor hours per dollar of sales fell 6% while the hourly wage rose 9.4%

claims.claim: Average hourly wage including benefits rose 9.4%, FY2023 to FY2025
evidence: From $16.80 to $18.38 an hour
State minimum-wage increases and a tight labor market, as the CFO and COO say
A further 4% minimum-wage rise is due in 2027, worth up to $7.3M a year

claims.claim: Labor hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6%
evidence: From 7.02 to 6.60 hours
Stores already run leaner than in FY2023, before any new cut
Managers in the leanest stores say produce rotation and receiving checks get skipped

claims.claim: Store labor as a share of sales changed 0.3 pp
evidence: From 11.8% to 12.1% of sales
The net effect of higher wages and fewer hours per dollar of sales
Explains 13% of the fall in operating margin, not most of it

slides.title: Why not cut store hours
Stores with the fewest labor hours lose the most to shrink, 3.1% of sales against 2.3% in the best-staffed quarter

claims.claim: Stores with the fewest labor hours lose the most to shrink
evidence: Shrink % of sales FY2025 by labor-hours quartile: Q1 fewest hours 3.1%; Q2 2.7%; Q3 2.4%; Q4 most hours 2.3%
Chain, FY2025 2.6%

claims.claim: Hours cut first into fresh and receiving
evidence: Q1: managers say produce rotation and receiving checks are skipped on busy days
fresh waste and receiving errors make up 65% of shrink, and both need staff time

claims.claim: Q3 to Q4: shrink barely moves, so the best-staffed quarter is where hours can come out safely
waste also signals weaker quality
evidence: Customers: 58% shop Harlow for fresh produce

claims.claim: Protect fresh and receiving hours in the leanest stores; trim only the best-staffed quarter

slides.title: If shrink rose as it did in FY2023–25, management's hour cut would keep only about half of its $14.5M saving

claims.claim: Management's hour cut would keep only about half of its $14.5M saving
evidence: $14.5M management's estimate of the annual saving from 8% fewer scheduled store hours
− $7.5M shrink rising another 0.5 percentage points of FY2025 sales, as it did when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6%
= $7M net annual saving, 48% of the plan's figure, before any lost sales

claims.claim: The estimate is cautious on four counts
evidence: The 8% cut is deeper than the 6% fall in hours that came with the last rise in shrink
The leanest quarter of stores already loses 3.1% of sales to shrink, compared with 2.6% for the chain
Lost sales from checkout waits and stock-outs are not counted, although 44% of customers come for convenience
Even the full $14.5M would lift operating margin only to about 2.0% of FY2025 sales, short of the 3.0% target

slides.title: Promotions and price
Promotions have grown more costly: they rose to 29% of sales while vendors funded a smaller share of markdowns

claims.claim: Promotions now carry 29% of sales, up from 24% in FY2023
evidence: +5 pp
Promotional share of sales: FY2023 24%; FY2024 26.2%; FY2025 29%

claims.claim: Vendors now fund less than half of each markdown dollar
evidence: −9 pp
Vendor funding % of promotional markdowns: FY2023 55%; FY2025 46%

claims.claim: Each percentage point of sales moved onto promotion costs Harlow 0.14 percentage points of margin
evidence: Promotional sales earn 14 percentage points less gross margin than regular-price sales, unchanged over the period

slides.title: Deeper promotions have not improved Harlow's price image, and customers come for fresh produce and convenience

claims.claim: More customers call Harlow expensive than before the promotions grew
evidence: +8 pp
Say Harlow is more expensive than other options: FY2023 33%; FY2025 41%
Customer survey, n = 3,100

claims.claim: Fresh produce, not price, is the top reason to shop at Harlow
evidence: Top reasons to shop, FY2025: Fresh produce 58%; Convenience 44%

claims.claim: Harlow stores near a new ValuMart: comparable sales of −4.2% in FY2025, against +1.1% elsewhere

slides.title: Cutting only money-losing events, back to 24% of sales, would add 0.7 percentage points of margin

claims.claim: Cutting only money-losing events, back to 24% of sales, would add 0.7 percentage points of margin
evidence: 5% of sales moves back to regular price, taking promotions from 29% to their FY2023 share of 24%
× 14 pp less gross margin on promotional sales than on regular-price sales
= 0.7 pp higher operating margin a year, about $9.9M on FY2028 sales

claims.claim: Why the cut can come from losing events alone
evidence: The 5% of sales is 17% of promotional sales, less than half of the 38% of FY2025 events that lost money even after their extra units
Sales moved off promotion stay with Harlow at regular price, and the margin gap of 14 percentage points holds
Promotions that defend traffic near ValuMart are reviewed event by event rather than cut
Not counted: recovering vendor funding from 46% toward the FY2023 level of 55% of markdowns

claims.claim: The category team's case measures sales, not profit
evidence: comparable sales of +1.8% in the deepest-promotion stores, against +0.2%

slides.title: E-commerce and home delivery
Counted in full, e-commerce lost about $10M in FY2025, not the profit its team reports

claims.claim: Counted in full, e-commerce lost about $10M in FY2025
evidence: $7.7M contribution from the 30% of $127.8M online sales that are new to Harlow, at 20 cents a dollar
− $9.8M picking: $7.40 for every online order
− $10.7M third-party delivery: $13.80 for each of the 58% of orders delivered
+ $2.4M delivery fees collected: $3.10 per delivered order
= −$10.4M e-commerce result in FY2025, before any store overhead

claims.claim: Two corrections turn the team's profit into a loss
evidence: Third-party delivery is counted; the team's 6.1% margin leaves it out because finance books it in fulfillment
Only new sales count: customers say they would otherwise have bought 70% of their online purchases in a Harlow store (survey of 2,300)
Contribution of 20 cents per new dollar is finance's estimate, before fulfillment
The rebuilt fulfillment cost matches the $18.1M reported for FY2025

slides.title: Home delivery drives the loss, with each delivered order costing $18.10 to fulfil and bringing only $5.76 of contribution

claims.claim: Home delivery drives the loss
evidence: Fulfillment cost per order, net of fees: Home delivery 18.1; Click-and-collect 7.4
Contribution from new sales per order: Home delivery 5.76; Click-and-collect 5.76
Share of the e-commerce loss from home delivery 91.2%

claims.claim: Free delivery on most baskets makes each delivered order a loss
evidence: Fees: delivery is free above $75 and the average basket is $96, so most delivered orders pay no fee
Mix: home delivery rose from 45% to 58% of orders, so the loss grew faster than online sales

claims.claim: Click-and-collect: costs only the picking and comes close to paying for itself
Contribution per order $5.8
evidence: $96 average online basket, FY2025 × 30% of each basket is new to Harlow (customer survey) × 20% contribution per new dollar (finance estimate) = $5.8

slides.title: Rolling out the tested delivery pricing would cut the loss by about $2.5M a year and keep the service customers expect

claims.claim: At a $7.99 fee, free only above $100: delivered orders in the test −9%
evidence: Fee test results (4 stores, 10 weeks, late FY2025)
Average fee collected rose from $3.10 to $6.40

claims.claim: Most customers switched rather than left
evidence: click-and-collect orders in the test 14%
Each switch saves the $13.80 delivery cost

claims.claim: A small loss of online sales
evidence: total e-commerce sales in the test −2%
Counted in full as lost to Harlow

claims.claim: Net gain of $2.5M a year if rolled out to all stores
evidence: Cuts the FY2025 e-commerce loss by about a quarter
$3M lower fulfillment cost: test changes applied to FY2025 orders
− $0.5M contribution lost on 2% fewer online sales, assuming none return to stores
= $2.5M net gain a year; delivery stays available to every customer

claims.claim: negotiate it alongside the roll-out
evidence: The provider proposed a 3% rate rise at the 2026 renewal, about $0.3M a year at tested volumes

slides.title: The plan and what comes first
Exiting the nine loss-making stores would add about $6.6M a year, and six can close at lease expiry by 2027

claims.claim: The nine stores with negative four-wall EBITDA, FY2025
evidence: −$3.1M four-wall EBITDA of the nine stores
On $118.0M of sales
9 of 58 stores lose money before overhead

claims.claim: 6 of the nine leases end by 2027: close at expiry, no vote
evidence: The other three need a board vote and $7.5M to exit
About $4.4M from the six at expiry

claims.claim: $6.6M gain a year from all nine exits
evidence: $3.1M four-wall loss removed
+ $3.5M contribution on the 25% of their $118.0M sales that moves to nearby stores, at 12%
= $6.6M annual gain to operating income from all nine exits

claims.claim: the gain to operating income is if anything understated
evidence: Four-wall EBITDA excludes depreciation and overhead

slides.title: Together, five moves would lift operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028, clearing the target before the 2027 wage rise

claims.claim: Five moves would lift operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028
evidence: 1.02% FY2025 operating margin
+ 0.97 pp promotions back to 24% of sales (0.70) and private label at its FY2023–25 pace (0.27)
+ 0.5 pp store hours: fixed fresh and receiving routines in the leanest half, 8% fewer hours in the best-staffed quarter
+ 0.5 pp exit of the nine loss-making stores, including the smaller sales base
+ 0.2 pp delivery repriced as tested
= 3.2% FY2028 operating margin on $1,412M of sales

claims.claim: What the estimate rests on
evidence: Sales of $1,412M: FY2025's $1,503M less sales lost from store exits and the delivery test, with no market growth
Operating income rises from $15.3M to about $44.9M; the only known one-time cost is the $7.5M of lease exits
Private label keeps gaining 0.75 percentage points of sales a year at its 12 percentage-point margin premium
Not included: the 2027 minimum-wage rise, up to $7.3M if every wage rose 4%, which would leave margin near 2.7%

slides.title: The five-move plan reaches the margin target that the hour cut misses, while protecting fresh and keeping home delivery

claims.claim: FY2028 operating margin: the deciding row
evidence: Management draft: About 2.0%: $15.3M plus the full $14.5M saving, on FY2025 sales
Recommended: About 3.2% before the 2027 wage rise
Labor explains 13% of the fall; the plan works on the other 87%

claims.claim: FY2026 covenant of $20M: Both can meet it
evidence: Management draft: Met if the full saving lands in FY2026
Recommended: Met if the first three moves deliver a quarter of their run-rate

claims.claim: Fresh produce and shrink: Plan protects fresh
evidence: Management draft: Cuts hours in the leanest stores too, where shrink is already 3.1%
Recommended: Fixes fresh routines in the leanest half; trims only the best-staffed quarter

claims.claim: Home delivery: Plan keeps the service
evidence: Management draft: Frozen at today's size; still loses about $10M a year
Recommended: Kept and repriced as tested; loss falls by $2.5M

claims.claim: Main risk: Plan's risks are sized
evidence: Management draft: Shrink and service erode half the saving
Recommended: Wage rise of up to $7.3M; ValuMart's response to fewer promotions

slides.title: Promotions, delivery pricing and store hours go first because they need no capital and can clear the FY2026 covenant

claims.claim: FY2028 gain by move
evidence: Promotions $9.9M (0.70 pp × $1,412M sales)
Store hours $6.8M (shrink $3.5M + hours $3.6M − $0.4M)
Store exits $6.6M (loss removed + moved sales)
Private label $3.8M (0.27 pp × $1,412M sales)
Home delivery $2.5M (tested fees on FY2025 orders)

claims.claim: Roadmap by fiscal half-year, FY2026 to FY2028
evidence: Promotions: Stop losing events; Renegotiate vendor funding
Home delivery: Tested fees; Renew contract
Store hours: Fresh routines; Trim top quarter
Private label: Range growth at today's pace
Store exits: Six at lease expiry; Three after board vote
Milestones: Covenant test; Board vote; 3.0% target

claims.claim: A quarter of the first three moves' $19.2M run-rate in FY2026 clears the $20M covenant

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Recommended: five moves — stop money-losing promotional events and return promotions to 24% of sales; roll out the tested delivery pricing ($7.99 fee, free above $100); replace the 8% across-the-board hour cut with fixed fresh and receiving routines in the leanest half and 8% fewer hours in the best-staffed quarter; exit the nine loss-making stores (six at lease expiry, three after a board vote); and grow private label at its FY2023–25 pace — lifting operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028. Promotions, delivery pricing and store hours go first because they need no capital and can clear the FY2026 covenant.

alternatives_considered.option: Management draft: 8% across-the-board cut in store hours, e-commerce frozen
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: would reach only about 2.0% operating margin even with the full $14.5M saving, short of the 3.0% target; a shrink rise like FY2023–25 would erase about half the saving ($7M net); cuts hours in the leanest stores where shrink is already 3.1%; delivery still loses about $10M a year. Can meet the FY2026 covenant if the full saving lands in FY2026.

alternatives_considered.option: Category team's case for deep promotions
alternatives_considered.treatment: Its evidence (comparable sales of +1.8% in the deepest-promotion stores, against +0.2%) measures sales, not profit.

alternatives_considered.option: Cutting promotions that defend traffic near ValuMart
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not cut; reviewed event by event rather than cut.
Free delivery on most baskets makes each delivered order a loss; replaced by tested pricing that keeps the service and saves about $2.5M a year.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: The 2027 minimum-wage rise, up to $7.3M a year, is the main risk to the plan; not included in the 3.2% estimate and would leave margin near 2.7%
ValuMart's response to fewer promotions is a risk
Sales of $1,412M: FY2025's $1,503M less sales lost from store exits and the delivery test, with no market growth
The only known one-time cost is the $7.5M of lease exits
Private label keeps gaining 0.75 percentage points of sales a year at its 12 percentage-point margin premium
Sales moved off promotion stay with Harlow at regular price, and the margin gap of 14 percentage points holds
Not counted: recovering vendor funding from 46% toward the FY2023 level of 55% of markdowns
Shrink rising another 0.5 percentage points of FY2025 sales under the 8% hour cut, as it did when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6%; lost sales from checkout waits and stock-outs not counted
Only 30% of online sales are new to Harlow (customer survey of 2,300); contribution of 20 cents per new dollar is finance's estimate
Delivery roll-out assumes none of the 2% lost online sales return to stores; provider proposed a 3% rate rise at 2026 renewal, about $0.3M a year
25% of the nine exited stores' $118.0M sales moves to nearby stores at 12% contribution; four-wall EBITDA excludes depreciation and overhead, so gain is if anything understated
FY2026 covenant is met if the first three moves deliver a quarter of their $19.2M run-rate
Timing follows the briefing pack, which treats FY2026 as the first plan year
Margins and gains are team estimates; data are synthetic benchmark data
next_steps: Stop the money-losing promotional events and cap promotions at 24% of sales; reopen vendor-funding talks — Chief merchandising officer — FY2026 H1
Roll out the tested delivery fee ($7.99, free above $100) to all stores and negotiate the 3% rate rise — Head of e-commerce, procurement — FY2026 H1
Replace the 8% across-the-board cut with fixed fresh and receiving routines and a trim in the best-staffed quarter — COO — FY2026 H1
Give notice on the six stores whose leases end by 2027; bring the other three to a board vote — CFO, real estate — Board vote FY2027 H1
Cost every move against the $25M cap and report monthly against the $20M covenant — CFO — Next board meeting
normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text with no images. I rebuilt the chart values on slide 4 from the stacked 'base' and 'Operating margin' series. The waterfall steps are the 'Operating margin' series values; I inferred the sign of each step (positive for private label, negative for the others) from the base values. On slides 5, 8, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19 and 21, the numbers and labels were extracted as separate lines, so I paired them up by their order on the slide. The roadmap on slide 21 lost its half-year positions in extraction, so I listed its milestones without timing. Slide 22 lists the next steps; I put them in next_steps rather than in the slide's claims.
